confusable_with.why: Implied consent means every driver has already agreed to be tested, while administrative revocation is what follows when the test is failed or refused.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: authored pedagogic emphasis (product policy), not an exam weight

confusable_with.why: A blood alcohol content above point zero five but below point zero eight makes a driver impaired, while point zero eight or more makes the driver under the influence.
The adult threshold for administrative revocation is point zero eight, while the zero tolerance threshold for drivers under twenty-one is point zero two.

A failed test and a refused test both trigger administrative revocation with a thirty-day temporary permit, while refusal adds a one, two or four year revocation based on prior alcohol enforcement contacts.
